Privacy Policy

Version 1.0 · effective March 1, 2026

Draft

We collect what the membership needs to function, and nothing we cannot explain in a sentence.

01

Information we collect

Account details you provide (name, email, membership tier, dependents where applicable), payment records held by our processor rather than by us, referral activity, donation history, and basic technical logs needed to keep the site secure.

02

How we use it

To operate your membership, verify referrals, administer scholarship applications, send the communications you have chosen, and meet our accounting and reporting obligations as a nonprofit.

03

Sharing and disclosure

We never sell member data. We share only what is necessary with our payment processor, email provider and, where an award is made, the recipient's institution. Partner organizations do not receive member lists.

04

Scholarship documents

Transcripts, enrolment proof and statements are requested only after eligibility is confirmed, are visible to the review committee alone, and are retained no longer than the cycle and our record-keeping obligations require.

05

Your rights

You may request an export of your data, correct inaccurate details, withdraw marketing consent, or ask for deletion of anything we are not required to retain. Requests are answered within thirty days.

06

Contact

Write to legal@sditraveltrust.org or the head office address in the footer. Where state law grants additional rights, those rights apply and this policy does not limit them.

Terms of Use

Version 1.0 · effective March 1, 2026

Draft

The directory is curated information, not an endorsement of any organization's performance.

01

Acceptable use

The site is for personal, non-commercial use by members and the public. Scraping the directory, reselling listings, or using member data for solicitation is prohibited and ends access.

02

Directory content

Listings are verified for licensing and contact accuracy at the time of review, but we do not control third parties. Any transaction you enter with a listed organization is between you and that organization.

03

Nothing on the site is legal, tax, immigration or financial advice. Travel requirements change; confirm anything consequential with the relevant government agency.

04

Intellectual property

The SDI Travel Trust name, logo and site content belong to us. Partner marks belong to their owners and appear with permission.

05

Limitation of liability

To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss arising from use of the site or reliance on a listing. Nothing here excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

06

Changes

We may update these terms; material changes are announced to members by email at least thirty days before they take effect.

Membership Terms

Version 1.0 · effective March 1, 2026

Draft

Twelve months, renewing annually, cancellable up to thirty days before the renewal date.

01

What membership includes

Directory access including member-only listings, travel industry and equipment resources, government agency information, partner offers, referral programme eligibility, and member communications. Family memberships extend these to dependent children aged 22 and under, subject to eligibility requirements.

02

Term and renewal

Memberships run for twelve months from the join date and renew annually on that anniversary at the then-current rate. We send a renewal notice thirty days beforehand.

03

Cancellation

Cancel at least thirty days before your renewal date from the Member Portal or by emailing membership@sditraveltrust.org. Cancellation stops the next charge; it does not shorten the current term.

04

Refunds

Dues are refundable within fourteen days of purchase if no member benefits have been used. Once the term has begun and benefits have been accessed, dues are non-refundable. Charitable donations are separate and generally non-refundable.

05

Upgrades and changes

Upgrade from Individual to Family at any time and pay the prorated difference for the remainder of the term. Referral points carry over unchanged.

06

Suspension

We may suspend or end a membership for abuse of the directory, misuse of partner offers, or fraudulent referral activity, with written notice and a pro-rata refund where the law requires one.

Referral Program Rules

Version 1.0 · effective March 1, 2026

Draft

Thirty points per confirmed referral. Confirmation follows a paid membership, not an invitation.

01

Eligibility

Active members in good standing may participate. Family households share one combined points balance regardless of who sent the referral.

02

Earning points

Each eligible referral earns thirty points once the referred person completes a paid membership within sixty days of using your link. Self-referrals, duplicate accounts and memberships that are refunded do not earn points.

03

Confirmation and disputes

Points appear as pending until the membership is paid and the payment has cleared. If a referral is missing, contact us within ninety days with the referred person's email and we will review the record.

04

Forfeiture

Points remain valid while your membership is active. If a membership lapses, points are forfeited after ninety days and are not reinstated by later renewal.

05

What points do

Points determine the maximum award level a candidate sponsored by you may be considered for. They are not currency, carry no cash value, cannot be transferred or sold, and do not guarantee an award.

06

Programme changes

We may adjust points, tiers or windows prospectively. Changes are announced to members and never reduce points already confirmed.

Scholarship Terms

Version 0.9 · effective Pending review

Draft

Reaching a tier sets the level a candidate may be considered for — it does not create an award.

01

Eligibility

An active sponsoring membership, points reaching the applied-for tier, enrolment or acceptance at an accredited institution, a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA or the institution's satisfactory-progress standard, complete documentation by the cycle deadline, and consent to verification. Board members, staff and their immediate families are not eligible.

02

Review and selection

Complete applications at an eligible tier are scored on published weighted criteria: financial need 35%, academic standing 25%, personal statement 25%, community involvement 15%. Referral points affect the eligible level only, never the score.

03

Funding limits

Each cycle spends only what the fund holds at close. Partial awards, fewer awards, or no award in a cycle are all possible outcomes, and reaching a tier confers no entitlement.

04

Disbursement

Where the institution permits it, awards are paid directly to the institution for the named term. Otherwise funds are paid to the recipient against documentation of educational use.

05

Tax treatment

Scholarship amounts may be taxable to the recipient depending on how they are used. We do not provide tax advice; recipients should consult their own adviser.

06

Pending review

Award timing, disbursement mechanics and state charitable-solicitation registrations remain under legal and tax review. This document will be revised before applications open.

Donation & Refund Policy

Version 1.0 · effective March 1, 2026

Draft

Charitable gifts are generally non-refundable, because the fund commits them to a cycle.

01

Acknowledgement

Every gift receives a written acknowledgement stating the amount and that no goods or services were provided in exchange, where that is the case. Membership dues are not treated as charitable contributions.

02

Non-refundable gifts

Donations are generally non-refundable once received. We will correct duplicate or mistaken transactions reported within thirty days.

03

Partner offer donations

A $25 or $50 partner donation is non-refundable once a discount code has been issued, since the benefit has been delivered. If a partner withdraws an offer before you use the code, we reissue or refund it.

04

Designations

Gifts may be designated to an award level or left unrestricted. Gifts cannot be earmarked for a named individual. Restricted gifts are tracked separately and reported annually.

05

Recurring gifts

Cancel or change a recurring gift at any time from the Member Portal or by email; changes take effect before the next scheduled charge.

Partner Disclosures

Version 1.0 · effective March 1, 2026

Draft

Placement is never purchased. Where money moves, the listing says so.

01

No paid placement

Directory inclusion is earned by review. No organization can pay for a listing, a category position, or preferential presentation.

02

Contributing partners

Some partners contribute to the scholarship fund per completed member booking, per qualifying purchase, or per policy issued. Each such listing carries that disclosure on its profile.

03

Fintech partners

Our fundraising fintech partner contributes a share of qualifying member transaction volume. Contribution rates and eligible merchant categories are published in the Member Portal.

04

Sponsors

Award sponsors are named in the announcement and annual summary. Sponsors have no role in eligibility, scoring or selection, and no access to applicant documents.

05

Government and nonprofit listings

Government resources and nonprofit peer organizations are listed with no relationship, endorsement or financial arrangement in either direction.

06

Removals

We remove listings for lapsed licensing, stale contact details, or an offer that stops being better than public pricing. Removals are not negotiable.

Financial Transparency

Version 1.0 · effective March 1, 2026

Draft

Sixty-two cents of every unrestricted dollar is allocated to the scholarship fund.

01

Allocation

Of each unrestricted dollar, 62¢ is allocated to the scholarship fund, 24¢ to directory curation and member programmes, and 14¢ to operations and administration. Restricted gifts are tracked and reported separately.

02

Review

The board reviews the fund and the allocation quarterly and approves any change to award levels. Staff hold no vote on scholarship decisions.

03

What we publish

An annual financial summary, the number and value of awards per cycle, the split of funding by channel, and the current allocation percentages.

04

Independent review

Financial statements are prepared annually and will be independently reviewed once the organization crosses the applicable state audit threshold.

05

Placeholders

Allocation percentages, award counts and totals shown across this site are placeholders pending audited figures for the first full year of operation.
